newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks mixed in morning, banks slump.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks mixed in morning, banks slump.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks traded mixed in morning trade on Tuesday, with banking stocks hammered after HSBC and Hang Seng Bank reported earnings on Monday but property stocks benefiting from some of that weakness, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index was down 25.25 points, or 0.19 percent, at 13,482.03. Turnover was HK$3.53 billion after the first hour of trade.
"For HSBC, people are selling on strength, and for Hang Seng Bank, people were surprised by the bank's results which grew very slowly," said Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities.
Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc fell HK$4.50 to HK$184.50 after the banking giant reported 1996 pretax profit of 4.52 billion stg compared with 3.67 billion.
Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities, said the bank was still an attractive global bank play.
"Investors will be happy to buy on weakness. People will start bargain-hunting on the Bank as we drift a little lower."
Shares in Hang Seng Bank Ltd tumbled HK$5.50 to HK$83.50. It posted a 6.3 percent rise in 1996 net profit to HK$8.49 billion. Analysts had expected a 16 percent rise.
Remington said there may be some downgrades on the stock.
Expectations of strong demand at forthcoming property sales boosted the sector on Tuesday morning. Analysts said the shares were also benefiting from weakness in the banking sector.
"As they move out of some of the stocks they have to buy something else so that will probably help the sector's performance," said Tsang.
"The developer stocks consolidated for a few month. A few months ago developers were trading at a big premium over net asset value but today some are trading at a discount," he added.
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd rose HK$0.75 to HK$77.50 and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd advanced HK$0.75 to HK$91.50.
Henderson Land Development Co Ltd rose HK$1.00 to HK$72.00.
"The whole sector has underperformed recently," said Remington.
Shares in China Aerospace International Holdings Ltd were up HK$0.10 at HK$2.775 after jumping to a record high of HK$2.85 on news the company would raise HK$535 million in a new share issue.
Elegance International Holdings Ltd rose HK$0.19 to HK$1.52. Italy's Safilo SpA has agreed to buy a 9.99 percent stake in the company.
